metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Waves — Electromagnetic Spectrum: Identifying Named Regions
metadata.note: Figure 5 shows a horizontal EM spectrum bar with regions from left (long wavelength/low frequency) to right (short wavelength/high frequency): A | Infrared | Visible light | B | X-rays | C. A = Microwaves, B = Ultraviolet, C = Gamma rays. 1 mark per correct identification. Word bank has 5 tokens (3 correct + 2 distractors).

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2023 Q4a — Electromagnetic Spectrum Regions
question.text:
The diagram below shows the electromagnetic spectrum. Three regions are labelled A, B, and C. Drag the correct name into each blank.

← longer wavelength   [[1]] | Infrared | Visible | [[2]] | X-rays | [[3]]   shorter wavelength →
question.general_feedback:
Electromagnetic spectrum (long wavelength → short wavelength):

Radio → Microwaves → Infrared → Visible → Ultraviolet → X-rays → Gamma rays

A = Microwaves (immediately to the left of infrared, lower frequency than visible light)
B = Ultraviolet (between visible light and X-rays — causes sunburn, detected by fluorescent materials)
C = Gamma rays (shortest wavelength, highest frequency — emitted by radioactive nuclei)

groups.label: EM region between radio waves and infrared (used for cooking)
groups.diagnostic_hint: MICROWAVES sit between radio waves and infrared. They are used in microwave ovens and mobile communications. Their wavelength is millimetres to centimetres.

groups.label: EM region between visible light and X-rays (causes sunburn)
groups.diagnostic_hint: ULTRAVIOLET (UV) radiation sits just above visible light in frequency. It causes tanning and sunburn, is used in sterilisation, and is blocked by ozone.

groups.label: EM region with highest frequency (nuclear emissions)
groups.diagnostic_hint: GAMMA RAYS have the highest frequency and energy of all EM radiation. They are emitted by radioactive nuclei and are used in cancer treatment and sterilisation.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 5 tokens for 3 slots. Radio waves: plausible distractor for A since both have longer wavelengths than infrared — tests whether students distinguish radio from microwave. Infrared: re-used as a distractor for B to catch students who confuse the ordering around visible light. The diagram already labels Infrared and X-rays, so students who read carefully should avoid placing them again.
